body: **Summary:** Metals companies are price-takers. Profit equals spread (steel price minus iron ore and coking coal; aluminium LME minus alumina and power) times volume, so returns are set by global supply (above all China) and cost-curve position. Miners (Coal India, NMDC, Hindustan Zinc) earn price minus mining cost and are high-dividend, cash-generative and policy-exposed. Key metrics: EBITDA/tonne, volume and capacity growth, spread over raw material, cost-curve position (captive ore and coal), net debt/EBITDA, capex intensity, free cash flow, and for Tata Steel, Europe losses. Cycle drivers: China production and exports (2015 and 2023–25 export floods), global PMI, Indian infrastructure demand, trade defence (12% safeguard duty on flat steel from 2025), coking coal prices, LME aluminium and energy costs, and the USD. Lead indicators: China steel exports and property starts (NBS), SGX iron ore and coking coal futures, JPC (Joint Plant Committee) Indian steel consumption, the LME, Indian HRC prices (SteelMint/BigMint), DGTR trade remedy notices, the global manufacturing PMI. Winners (JSW on low-cost growth, Hindalco via Novelis downstream, Hindustan Zinc on cost leadership) had captive raw materials, the lowest cost quartile, and countercyclical balance sheets. Losers bought abroad at peak (Tata Corus 2007) or leveraged up into the downcycle (Essar, Bhushan, Monnet in 2015–17 IBC). Valuation: EV/EBITDA 4–8x on mid-cycle and P/B 0.7–2.5x. Buy when P/E is high or negative at the trough; sell when P/E is low at peak margins. Nov 2026: Q2 FY27 was strong (Tata Steel India PAT ₹5,055 cr, crude steel 6.21 mt +10%; JSW PAT ₹5,359 cr, EBITDA margin ~18.6%), and CLSA sees H2 FY27 momentum. Traps: low P/E at peak spreads. Sources: [1](https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/business/4003265-tata-steel-reports-rs-5055-crore-net-profit-in-india-business-for-q2fy27) · [2](https://www.psuconnect.in/financial/jsw-steel-q2-results-record-production-sales-consolidated-pat-at-5-359-cr) · [3](https://www.constructionworld.in/amp/steel-news/indian-steel-industry-poised-for-volume-led-recovery-in-h2fy27/96585) · [4](https://www.icra.in/Research/ViewResearchReport/ferrous-metals-sector/7091)

Flag: CLEAN. 120-year-old Chennai family group run through Ambadi Investments (unlisted holdco) and professional CEOs. Listed: Cholamandalam Investment & Finance, Cholamandalam Financial Holdings, Tube Investments of India, Carborundum Universal, Coromandel International, EID Parry, CG Power (acquired by TII in 2020 after the Thapar-era fraud there), Shanthi Gears, Wendt. Minority record: no meaningful promoter pledging, conservative leverage, consistent dividends; the CG Power rescue (TII infused capital, cleaned up books after the previous management's undisclosed liabilities and RPTs) is a positive governance case that created large value for TII holders. Main blemish: a 2019-2023 family dispute -- Valli Arunachalam (daughter of late chairman M.V. Murugappan) sought an Ambadi board seat; family policy of no women on the holdco board drew criticism. Settled out of court Aug-2023; the family said the settlement did not involve the listed companies. Holdco structure (Cholamandalam Financial Holdings) trades at a discount. Status Nov-2026: no regulator orders found; a group widely regarded as a governance benchmark among Indian family groups.

- **red flags:** 2019-23 family dispute (settled, outside listed cos); holdco discount
- **good conduct:** CG Power cleanup; conservative leverage; professional management

On a P/E of 52, about a quarter of the "E" is treasury and group rent and dividends.
- **The labour-code charge (₹94.2 cr) is a one-time catch-up** on gratuity and leave under the new "wages" definition, presented as exceptional `[Q2R n.6]`. The *recurring* part shows up as employee cost +18% YoY in Q2 FY27 (§4.4).
- **Customer concentration jumped.** **Three external customers = ₹3,734.7 cr = 30.8% of sales** (FY25: two customers, ₹2,226.8 cr = 21.5%) `[AR26 consolidated n.44]`. Each is ≥10% of revenue (≥ ~₹1,214 cr). CIL sells power-gen engines through *three* GOEMs, so the three customers are **very likely the three GOEMs** [EST; inference, unverified]. The third one crossing 10% fits DC growth flowing through a GOEM.
- **Debt:** borrowings ₹37 cr (leases only); cash and MFs ~₹3,800–4,000 cr ("INR 38–40 billion", analyst on the call `[CC-Q2FY27]`; AR: MFs ₹1,360 cr + other liquid ₹689 cr + deposits).

**The adjustment that matters:** Q2 FY26 GAAP operating income was $275.4M, of which **$163.6M was an IEEPA tariff refund credited to COGS**. That is 13.0% of the quarter's sales. GAAP diluted EPS was $3.99, adjusted EPS $1.68 `[PR-Q2 FY26]`. The FY26 GAAP EPS guide of $12.10–12.58 against an adjusted guide of $9.83–10.31 carries the same one-off. **Any screen that reads trailing GAAP EPS or GAAP gross margin for FIVE over the next four quarters is wrong by ~$2.3 per share.** This is a textbook "good-but-misleading" row (§8).
